label: ePrivacy Directive Art. 5 — Confidentiality of communications
body: 3. Member States shall ensure that the use of electronic communications networks to store information or to gain access to information stored in the terminal equipment of a subscriber or user is only allowed on condition that the subscriber or user concerned is provided with clear and comprehensive information … and is offered the right to refuse such processing. This shall not prevent any technical storage or access for the sole purpose of carrying out or facilitating the transmission of a communication … or as strictly necessary in order to provide an information society service explicitly requested by the subscriber or user.

Note: the 2009 amendment under Directive 2009/136/EC re-interprets "offered the right to refuse" as a prior, freely given, informed consent requirement (the "cookie consent" rule). GDPR Art. 4(11) supplies the consent standard.
